title: Closed-network deployment operational contract and canary scenario spec
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
PRD summary:
This ticket captures the operational contract and acceptance criteria for deploying Redwood Private into closed (air-limited / fully isolated) networks. The goal is to define a predictable, testable rollout and upgrade pattern that operators (customer ops & Redwood SRE) can follow with deterministic rollback windows and measurable safety gates.

Context and motivation:
- Several regulated customers require zero- or minimal-egress deployments and strict upgrade controls. Existing acceptance docs cover bootstrap and offline artifact sync, but we lack a concise operator-facing contract that ties networking constraints to canary traffic patterns, telemetry expectations, and rollback thresholds.
- This PRD bridges product acceptance, SRE runbooks, and upgrade automation so a single checklist can be validated during onboarding and upgrades.

Non-goals:
- Redesigning the operator UI or implementing a new operator. This is an operational contract and spec; implementation tickets will be created for automation and operator code changes.
- Replacing existing artifact signing or image provenance work (those are complementary and tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Deployment can bootstrap from a local mirror with zero external egress (0 outbound connections) using signed artifacts and documented staging commands.
Operator can perform a staged upgrade (canary -> partial -> global) with automated health checks; canary cohorts must be configurable by node label and region.
Telemetry: control-plane and data-plane heartbeats must emit to the local telemetry collector within 60s of startup; missing heartbeats for >5mins triggers automatic rollback to previous image.
SLOs: during canary (up to 5% instances) tail latency 99th percentile must remain within 1.5x baseline; customer-facing error rate must be <0.5% during any rollout window.
Rollback criteria: any canary producing >0.5% error rate OR sustained 99p latency >2x baseline for 2 consecutive 10m windows triggers automated rollback and operator notification.
Upgrade offline validation: checksum reconciliation of staged artifacts must succeed on all nodes before switching traffic; mismatch halts rollout and demotes to manual remediation.
Operator checklist: documented pre-flight checks (NTP, DNS split-horizon, CNI MTU, image mirror reachable) must be runnable as a single script and return a non-zero exit on failed checks.
Audit logs: every upgrade must produce an operator audit event stored locally and replayable to Redwood support during troubleshooting (minimum retention: 90 days).
rollout_plan: 1) Pre-flight: run local preflight script, collect artefact checksums, snapshot operator state. 2) Mirror verification: ensure artifact mirror responds and checksums match. 3) Canary: deploy to 1-2 control-plane nodes and 1 small data-plane cohort (<=5% of capacity). 4) Monitor: 30 minute hold with automated health, log, and metric checks. 5) Partial rollout: expand to 25% cohorts in staggered waves (10m spacing). 6) Full rollout: remaining nodes in 30m waves with automated canary rollback guards. 7) Post-upgrade validation: run traffic-replay test suite and snapshot telemetry for 72h. Specific timings can be shortened by mutual agreement with customer in the runbook.
test_matrix: Scenario A - Zero-egress bootstrap: fresh cluster boots from on-prem mirror; expected: completed bootstrap within 45min, no external DNS queries observed.
Scenario B - Canary failure injection: introduce transient CPU spike on canary nodes; expected: rollout pauses and rolls back if error rate threshold exceeded.
Scenario C - Mirror mismatch: corrupt a staged artifact; expected: checksum reconciliation detects mismatch and halts rollout with alert.
Scenario D - Network partition: simulate split-horizon DNS misconfiguration; expected: pre-flight detects DNS mismatch and blocks upgrade.
Scenario E - NTP drift: >5s drift injected; expected: preflight warns and upgrade blocked until corrected.
Scenario F - Airgap upgrade via physical media: validate import and signature verification flows for offline artifact ingestion.
decisions: Decision 2025-02-18: prefer staged canary by node label over per-customer traffic slicing due to operator simplicity and existing node-label workflows.
Decision 2025-02-21: require local telemetry sink + short-term retention as a minimum for auditability; long-term export is optional and handled by customer policies.
Trade-off: tight offline upgrade windows increase operational burden for customers; mitigated via vendor-provided preflight tooling and clear runbooks.
Security: artifact signing and signature verification remain mandatory; we will not support unsigned offline upgrades.
